title: Applied Scientist, Product Policy Research & Measurement
description:
About the Team

The Product Policy team develops and implements policies that shape how OpenAI’s technology is built and used. We work with teams across the company to turn complex questions about AI’s benefits and risks into practical guidance for responsible research, product development, and deployment.

About the Role

We are hiring a senior applied scientist to study how AI affects people and society using OpenAI production data, experiments, and social science methods. This role sits at the intersection of applied social science, AI, and product policy. The scientist will own research from an ambiguous question through study design, data collection and analysis, methodological validation, and recommendations. Their work will inform product and policy decisions and, where appropriate, contribute to external publications. We are looking for a hands-on empirical social scientist with exceptional methodological judgment.

In this role, you will:

- Develop and execute a research agenda on AI’s social impact, including effects on well-being, learning, social connection, trust, and human decision-making, in partnership with product and policy teams.

- Own empirical studies end to end: define the question and estimand, choose the design, build the dataset, conduct the analysis, and explain what the evidence supports.

- Analyze large-scale production and behavioral data, linking them to experiments, surveys, or external outcomes when appropriate to measure real-world effects.

- Design randomized experiments and credible observational studies; test identification assumptions, quantify uncertainty, and distinguish association from causal effects.

- Develop and validate measures of social outcomes, including human and LLM-assisted annotations; assess measurement error, subgroup performance, and drift.

- Translate findings into concrete product and policy recommendations, with clear limits on causal interpretation, generalizability, and decision confidence.

- Partner with Product Policy, Research, Product, Data Science, Engineering, UXR, Legal, and domain experts; contribute rigorous work to external publications when appropriate.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

- A PhD or equivalent research experience in sociology, political science, psychology, communication, computational social science, or a related empirical field, with demonstrated independent research ownership.

- Deep expertise in research design, causal inference, experimentation, statistical analysis, and measurement, demonstrated through work you can personally explain and defend.

- Strong SQL and Python or R skills, with experience independently constructing and analyzing complex behavioral datasets and producing reproducible research.

- A record of research that informs consequential decisions about technology and people, with the judgment to identify both useful findings and unresolved uncertainty.

- Clear writing for technical and policy audiences, and experience producing rigorous research papers or equivalent public technical work.

- The ability to move quickly, collaborate across functions, and maintain scientific independence when findings are sensitive or inconvenient.

About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

• Design clear benchmarks and measurements, accounting for tradeoffs among throughput, latency, resource use, and the quality or correctness of results.

• Partner with workload owners to understand requirements, test improvements, and help deploy solutions.

• Independently prioritize and drive optimization projects from investigation through measurable results.

• Experience analyzing and improving the performance of compute-intensive software

• Understanding of GPU architecture and the factors that affect utilization and application performance.

• Experience using profiling, benchmarking, and measurement to guide optimization decisions.

• Ability to work independently, communicate findings clearly, and collaborate with researchers and engineers.

• Three or more years of relevant experience.

• Optimizing AI training, inference, evaluation, or other large-scale GPU workloads.

• Working with GPU programming or machine learning frameworks and performance tools.

• Improving workload scheduling, batching, data pipelines, or multi-GPU configurations.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Inference Routing
description:
About PolarGrid
PolarGrid is an early-stage Canadian company that runs managed AI inference. Customers bring their own models, and we run them as fast, reliable production endpoints on GPU servers across many sites. We are a small team of about five engineers.
The role
You will own the routing layer: the service that decides which GPU serves each request. You will build it, run it in production and set its technical direction.
This is a hands-on staff role. Most of your time goes to designing and writing the router and the placement logic behind it. You will work closely with the engineers who run our network and our GPU sites, and you will help hire the engineers who join you.
The work
Every request has to land on a GPU that is healthy, has room and is close enough to be fast. The hard part is that capacity and health change constantly across many sites, and the router has to make good decisions quickly with information that is always slightly out of date. It also has to fail safely: when a site or server goes down, traffic moves without customers noticing.
What you bring

• Deep knowledge of how networks, proxies and load balancers work underneath, from building or running production systems.

• Strong distributed systems fundamentals: consistency, failure handling, retries and backpressure.

• You write production code in a systems language such as Go or Rust.

• You measure latency at the tail, not just the average, and know how to find where it comes from.

• You have been on call for what you built.

• You have set technical direction that other engineers built on.

• You write clearly.

• You use AI tools well and check their work.

You do not need GPU or ML experience. What matters is that you understand the systems underneath deeply and want to build a new one from the start.

description:
About Forterra

At Forterra , we are unleashing autonomy at scale to transform the battlefield. Our mission is to build the foundational platforms that enable an intelligent ecosystem to coordinate, adapt, and execute with speed and precision even in the uncertainty and disruption of modern conflict. In an era marked by rapid technological change and evolving threats, we design for flexibility, survivability, and operational dominance.

Forterra delivers weapons, sensors, and battlefield effects through integrated autonomous networks reaching operational areas faster, safer, and without placing human lives at risk. Our systems operate with distributed control, dynamic routing, and real-time responsiveness, enabling sustained advantage across complex mission environments.

About the role

Forterra is looking for a Lead Software Test Engineer to establish and run verification and validation for the safety critical embedded software used on our autonomous ground vehicles. This is initially an individual contributor role. You will set the software test approach, build the automation and test environments, execute the work, and maintain the evidence needed for customer and safety reviews. You will work closely with software, systems, and safety engineers to find problems early and make sure the software behaves correctly when things go wrong. As the capability grows, the role may develop into a technical lead for a small test team

Someone who can build a practical software test capability from the ground up and is comfortable working directly in the code, test environments, and evidence. This person should be able to work across software, systems, and safety engineering while staying focused on finding meaningful failures and making the product more dependable

What you'll do

• Set the verification and validation approach for safety critical embedded software from kickoff through qualification, including the test plan, test procedures, results, and reports.

• Turn system, software, and safety related requirements into practical tests with objective pass or fail criteria.

• Maintain traceability between requirements, tests, results, and anomalies.

• Build and maintain automated test frameworks for embedded software, including software in the loop and hardware in the loop environments.

• Exercise failure behavior through fault injection, timing and jitter tests, communications failures, memory faults, power and clock faults, negative tests, boundary tests, and stress tests.

• Use static analysis, dynamic analysis, and coverage results to find gaps and help the team close them.

• Prepare and maintain test evidence, including plans, procedures, results, V&V matrices, compliance matrices, anomaly records, tool qualification records, and contributions to the safety case.

• Work with software, systems, and safety engineers to review designs for testability, improve requirements, and support technical reviews and assessments.

• Provide technical guidance through test plan reviews, design reviews, pairing, and mentoring.

• Help establish the practices and infrastructure needed to grow a small software test capability.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Equivalent experience may be considered.

• Five or more years of experience testing embedded systems or safety critical software.

• Strong working knowledge of C or C++ and Python for test automation.

• Experience working with requirements management and requirements traceability using tools such as Jama or DOORS.

• Familiarity with MISRA C or MISRA C++, static analysis, and structural coverage methods such as branch coverage and MC/DC.

• Experience testing software on an RTOS such as QNX, including work with embedded targets, debuggers, and instrumentation.

• Strong troubleshooting skills and the ability to separate hardware, software, and firmware problems in a complex system.
